title: Green Anarkali for a Wedding Guest: Mehndi to Reception 2026
excerpt: A green Anarkali works at almost every wedding function. See which greens suit mehndi or evening, and how to pair them with gold or silver jewellery.
body:
*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. Our gota and embroidery work is done by hand in our own Jaipur unit.*

A green Anarkali is a smart choice for a wedding guest because green works from morning to night: choose mint, sage or parrot green for the mehndi and daytime events, and emerald or bottle green for the sangeet and reception. Pair lighter greens with silver and deeper greens with gold. This guide is for guests abroad planning outfits for a wedding this season.

## Why is green a lucky colour at Indian weddings?

Green is linked with new beginnings, growth and prosperity across many Indian communities, which is why you see it so often at mehndi ceremonies. In some regions, such as Maharashtra, green glass bangles are part of bridal tradition, and family members often wear green to share in the celebration.

It is also a practical colour for guests. Green rarely competes with the bride's red, it flatters most skin tones, and it looks rich in photos whether you are in a sunny garden or a hotel ballroom.

## Which shade of green works for which function?

The rule is simple: lighter greens for daytime, deeper greens for evening.

| Green shade | Best function | Fabric | Jewellery | Why it works |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mint | Mehndi, puja | Block print cotton | Silver or pearl | Fresh in daylight |
| Sage | Mehndi, day reception | Taffeta silk | Gold or polki | Soft but dressy |
| Parrot or lime | Mehndi, haldi | Cotton | Silver | Bright and playful |
| Olive | Puja, family lunch | Embroidered cotton | Oxidised silver | Earthy and easy |
| Bottle green or emerald | Sangeet, reception | Silk, georgette | Gold or kundan | Rich under night lights |

If you have a warm undertone, olive, sage and bottle green look especially good. Cool undertones suit emerald and mint. Almost everyone can wear a mid-tone sage.

## Which green outfits should you choose?

### For the reception: a sage taffeta Anarkali with gota

Taffeta silk holds a beautiful structure, and gota work catches every light in the room. Our [sage green taffeta silk Anarkali with gota work and a sequin organza dupatta](/products/sage-green-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-sequin-organza-dupatta/) at $52 is dressy enough for an evening reception and soft enough in colour for a daytime one.

### For the sangeet: bottle green with movement

A deep bottle green kurta or Anarkali looks striking on the dance floor. The [bottle green embroidered kurti with side tie-up](/products/green-embroidered-kurti/) at $25 is an easy base. Pair it with flared pants and a gold dupatta for a sangeet, or with palazzos for a relaxed dinner.

### For the mehndi or puja: mint block print

Mint is the softest way to wear green at a daytime event. The [mint green hand block print kurta set with a hand work yoke](/products/mint-green-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-dupatta-set-with-hand-work-yoke/) at $48 is breathable cotton, comfortable on the floor while the henna dries, and fresh in photos.

### For the travel day or family lunch: olive

Not every moment of a wedding week is a function. The [olive green embroidered cotton tunic with a white floral yoke](/products/olive-green-white-embroidered-cotton-tunic-top/) at $27 pairs with jeans or white pants for the airport, a family lunch or a casual welcome dinner.

## Should you wear gold or silver jewellery with green?

Both work. The choice depends on the shade and the time of day:

- **Gold** warms up bottle green, emerald, olive and sage, and looks rich at night
- **Silver or oxidised** suits mint, parrot and lime, and keeps daytime looks light
- **Kundan or polki** adds glamour to a sage or emerald reception look
- **Pearls** soften any green and work across functions
- **Red or pink accents**, like a potli or bangles, make green pop in photos

Avoid too many colours at once. Green with one accent colour, such as pink, gold or ivory, looks balanced. Green with pink, orange and blue together can feel busy.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Gota is a metallic ribbon work traditionally used in Rajasthan, and it shines softly rather than glaring. On a sage taffeta base, it catches warm stage lights and candlelight beautifully. On cotton, we keep the hand work fine near the neckline so the green stays the hero.

## How do you style a green outfit for each body and setting?

If the wedding is in a cold city, such as Toronto or London in December, a deep green looks lovely with a cream or gold shawl over it. In a warm venue like Dubai or a Sydney summer wedding, lighter greens in cotton or chanderi keep you cool.

For hair and makeup, green suits warm bronze or soft pink lips. A gold or kohl eye adds drama for the evening. Keep shoes neutral, like gold, nude or tan juttis, so the colour carries the look.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is green a good colour for an Indian wedding guest?**
Yes. Green is considered auspicious, rarely clashes with the bride and works from daytime mehndi to an evening reception.

**What colour dupatta goes with a green Anarkali?**
Gold, ivory, pink or peach all work well. A pink or gold dupatta on bottle green is a classic, festive pairing.

**Can I wear green to a mehndi if the bride is wearing green?**
Usually yes, but choose a different shade, such as sage if she is in parrot green, and keep your embellishment lighter than hers.

**How do I store a taffeta silk Anarkali after the wedding?**
Fold it in a cotton or muslin cloth, not plastic, and keep it away from damp. Refold it every few months so the creases do not set.
